lane_impact: L-combat-core: the stance triangle is a x1.2 multiplier applied BEFORE defense subtraction, and the behead x1.5 is applied AFTER the minimum-damage clamp — an ordering no ledger holds and one that changes low-damage outcomes materially. quote: MCSPlayer.as `if(this.stance == LIGHT_STANCE && enemyStance == BALANCED_STANCE || this.stance == BALANCED_STANCE && enemyStance == HEAVY_STANCE || this.stance == HEAVY_STANCE && enemyStance == LIGHT_STANCE) { damage *= 1.2; ... }` then `damage -= this.getDefense();` then `if(damage < damageObj.getMinDamage()) { damage = damageObj.getMinDamage(); }` then `if(behead) { damage *= 1.5; }` then `gotHitCounter = 12;`

quote: §1t1541s0§.as:51 `internal static var maxDistance:int = 200;` · :106-108 `public static function §1t10094s0§(param1:int) : * { maxDistance = param1; }` · §1t99s0§.as:3158 `§1t1541s0§.§1t10094s0§(this.§1t4417s0§);` inside setStance · §1t1523s0§.as:2347 `return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));`
text: InputManager.maxDistance = 200 is a compile-time initialiser, not a gameplay base. setStance calls InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength) on every battle init for the local player (web §1t99s0§.as:3156-3158, android MCSPlayer.as:3092-3094), so the 200 is overwritten before the player ever draws a stroke. Any derivation of the wiki's 300/200/100 that treats 200 as 'the shipped default slash budget' rests on a value the player never plays at. The real base is 120 + floor((90 + 5*DAN) * SPD / (20 + SPD)) — 124 at SPD 1 / dan 0, asymptotically 210 at dan 0.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core — closes the open question the packet honestly left STILL_UNHELD (combat-core/mastery-domain). Mastery is the raw 1-10 skill level; no rescale, no INFERRED flag needed, as long as the coefficients are taken from the web build.
text: The stance-mastery domain is RESOLVED as the skilldata 1-10 <value>, and the WEB coefficients are built for it. Player masteries are getStat(1000)/getStat(1001)/getStat(1002) passed straight into initPlayer; NPC masteries are the npcdata <lvl> returned verbatim by XMLNpc.getMastery. On the web coefficients (0.2*m*0.1 = 0.02 per level, 0.4*m*0.1 = 0.04 per level) that domain gives a real spread — Balanced 1.02→1.20, Heavy 0.54→0.90 — so no 0-100 conversion exists or is needed. The android build's 0.5*m*0.01 form is the anomaly that made the domain look broken.
